paper.title: The enlightening role of explainable artificial intelligence in medical & healthcare domains: A systematic literature review

evidence.paraphrase: The review concerns explainability of machine-learning predictions and clinical decisions in medical and healthcare applications.
Its human-facing contribution is trust in model predictions through feature-importance explanations, not control of literature retrieval or curation.

reviews.rationale: The abstract addresses XAI for medical prediction rather than a scholarly search, recommendation, or evidence-selection workflow. Explainability alone does not make it evidence for governance of literature curation.

paper.title: IdeaSynth: Iterative Research Idea Development Through Evolving and Composing Idea Facets with Literature-Grounded Feedback

evidence.paraphrase: IdeaSynth uses literature-grounded feedback to help researchers iteratively develop and compose facets of research ideas.
The reported evaluations measure exploration and elaboration of ideas, not human oversight of literature selection, provenance, or retrieval feedback loops.

reviews.rationale: The contribution is an LLM-supported research-ideation interface, with literature serving as grounding for feedback. The abstract does not describe bibliographic curation, selection overrides, provenance, or governance of a scholarly retrieval state.

paper.title: REIMAGINING INTELLIGENT INFORMATION SYSTEMS: EMERGING AI PARADIGMS IN LIBRARY AND INFORMATION SCIENCE

evidence.paraphrase: The paper broadly advocates human-centred, ethical governance of AI-driven knowledge systems in library and information science.
Its theory synthesis discusses information retrieval and scholarly communication but specifies no interactive literature-selection workflow, provenance control, or feedback-loop safeguard.

reviews.rationale: The paper has broad thematic overlap with human-centred governance in LIS, but the abstract is too general to support the assigned evidence role. It does not evaluate or define human control over literature curation or recommendation.

evidence.paraphrase: The article synthesizes scholarship on past, theoretical, fictional, and climate-related forms of societal collapse.
It uses literature review as a study method but does not study literature search, recommendation, curation, or governance.

reviews.rationale: This is a domain review of societal collapse, not research on the process or governance of bibliographic selection. The phrase literature review is a lexical match only.

paper.title: A Survey on Conversational Search and Applications in Biomedicine

evidence.paraphrase: The survey treats conversational search as an information-retrieval process in which users interact through dialogue during information-seeking tasks.
It emphasizes human-interactive characteristics across retrieval, question-answering, and recommender action modules.
The abstract situates the application in biomedical and healthcare information seeking rather than explicitly in scholarly literature curation.

reviews.rationale: The human-dialogue control of retrieval and recommendation is a relevant bridge mechanism for interactive curation. Its contribution is not specific to scholarly bibliography governance, so it supports the role indirectly rather than as a direct literature-curation precedent.
